validity.recommendation: Existence, classification (interstate offshore Gulf of Mexico gas gathering/transmission pipeline), and duplicate status are all clear -- no changes needed there. But the sheet's Length (325 mi) and Capacity (1200 MMcf/d) need re-verification against the pipeline's CURRENT (post-2023) configuration: Stingray Pipeline Company, L.L.C. (FERC Docket CP20-529-000, filed 2020-09-25, amended after Hurricane Delta) was authorized by FERC (order issued 2023-06-15, rehearing denied 2023-08-17, D.C. Circuit review denied 2024-12-20, Case No. 23-1288) to abandon by sale to Triton Gathering LLC approximately 172.98 miles of pipeline -- including about 103 miles of the 36-inch mainline, the 8,500-hp CS 701 compressor station, and the West Cameron 148 platform -- PLUS its entire NGA Sec.7 certificate, blanket certificates, and FERC gas tariff. Stingray retained only Segment 3394 (~25 mi, 30-in, Hurricane Delta-damaged, out of service since 2020), which FERC conditioned continued abandonment on restoring to service or reaching agreement with shipper ERT. This is corroborated in the BOEM route geometry: of the 45 pipeline-segment features on file for P0256, about 30 are coded ABN/PABN/REM (abandoned/pending-abandoned/removed) and only a minority remain ACT (active) -- but 42 of the 45 features are still attributed to 'Stingray Pipeline Company, L.L.C.' itself (SDE_COMPAN field), NOT to other operators, so this is Stingray's OWN abandonment history baked into the federal dataset, not route contamination from unrelated pipelines' laterals. Recommend: (a) do not change Status (still 'operating' -- Energy Transfer's own April-2025 Pipeline Safety Info public-awareness filing still lists 'Stingray Pipeline' as an active DOT-regulated natural-gas line in Cameron Parish, LA, consistent with the retained/restored Segment 3394 and any facilities NOT sold to Triton); (b) flag Length=325 mi and Capacity=1200 MMcf/d as likely STALE for the current (post-sale) system -- historical 1972-74 construction sources put the original design at 255.7 mi planned / ~228 mi actually laid by Sept. 1974 with a design capacity 'slightly in excess of 1 Bcf/d' (roughly 1,000-1,100 MMcf/d), neither of which matches 325 mi / 1200 MMcf/d, and the intervening ~50 years plus the 2020s abandonment of ~173 mi make it very unlikely the current physical system is still 325 mi. No source found stating a precise CURRENT total mileage or capacity for the post-abandonment system.
